summary.intent: Debug a broken statusline and Stop-hook error, update GSD, clean up stale worktrees, then plan and execute Phase 61 (AAD-Bound Seal Primitive and Cross-Language KAT) of the CipherBox project.
summary.outcome: Fixed statusline (ESM/CJS conflict), restored a broken GSD install by upgrading to 1.6.0 (restoring gsd-context-monitor.js), removed 3 stale worktrees, produced 5 verified PLAN.md files across 4 waves for Phase 61, and executed Waves 1–3 (196 tests green, C-01 merge gate closed on both TS and Rust); Wave 4 was dispatched but the transcript ends before completion.

repo: package.json has `"type": "module"` — Node treats all .js files as ESM; any CommonJS hook (e.g. GSD statusline, gsd-context-monitor) must use the .cjs extension or it crashes with 'require is not defined'.

GSD hooks are gitignored via `.gitignore:55` (`gsd-*` glob), so they are not persisted across clones or branch switches — the main-tree GSD install was a broken fragment while worktrees had complete 1.4.3 installs.

vitest `include: ['src/**/*.ts']` only discovers tests under `packages/crypto/src/__tests__/`; the path `packages/crypto/__tests__/build-node-aad.test.ts` cited in CONTEXT.md and ROADMAP.md would never be discovered.

`scripts/check-vector-parity.sh` has a hardcoded `EXPECTED_VECTORS` array — any new vector file (e.g. `node-aad.json`) must be registered there or the parity CI step fails even when both TS and Rust tests pass.

`sealAesGcmAad` mints a fresh random IV and cannot produce a fixed test output; fixed-IV KAT vectors must target the lower-level `encryptAesGcmAad`/`decrypt_aes_gcm_aad` directly (same pattern as existing `aes-gcm.json` targeting `encrypt_aes_gcm`).
`uuid` crate (v1.23.4) is the only new workspace dependency introduced in Phase 61; it was not previously in `Cargo.toml` or `crates/crypto/Cargo.toml`.
Dead-code warnings from `crates/fuse`/`metadata.rs` are pre-existing noise from the workspace build, unrelated to Phase 61's `crates/crypto` changes.
GSD worktrees under `.claude/worktrees/` are disposable (gitignored, regeneratable via GSD install); the 1.4.3 installs inside them were safely removed.
The GSD commit helper consistently false-negatives — reports failure when the commit actually landed; always verify with `git log` immediately after.

code.finding: This path is wrong — CONTEXT.md and ROADMAP.md reference it but vitest `include: ['src/**/*.ts']` will never discover it. Correct path: `packages/crypto/src/__tests__/build-node-aad.test.ts`.
Renamed to statusline.cjs to force CommonJS treatment; repo `"type": "module"` caused `require` to throw as ESM, silently blanking the statusline.
Project-level `statusLine` command updated to reference `statusline.cjs` after the rename.

TS AAD KAT acceptance criteria hardened to add `expect(vectors.aad_vectors).toHaveLength(4)` plus role-set assertion `expect(vectors.aad_vectors.map(v=>v.role).sort()).toEqual([1,2,3,4])` to prevent vacuous pass if role vectors are silently dropped.
Rust AAD KAT acceptance criteria pinned to `assert_eq!(aad_vectors.len(), 4)` to match the TS count guard and prevent silent erosion of four-role coverage.

TS seal KAT acceptance criteria hardened with `expect(vectors.seal_vectors.length).toBeGreaterThan(0)` to prevent vacuous pass on empty seal_vectors, matching the Rust `!seal_vectors.is_empty()` guard.
One file with two keyed arrays (`aad_vectors` + `seal_vectors`) rather than two files — frozen in Wave 1 with all four role-byte vectors [1,2,3,4].

workflow: Ultracode multi-lens adversarial plan review (plan-checker + 3 crypto lenses) caught a vacuous-pass hole in vector array KAT assertions that the standard plan-checker alone missed — worth running for security-critical crypto phases.
Adversarial verification converged in 2 rounds: round 1 found blockers, auto-revision via planner fixed them, round 2 passed with zero remaining blockers.
Unsigned commits must be configured locally (`git config commit.gpgsign false`) for AFK subagent sessions when 1Password SSH signing requires biometric approval — otherwise every commit hangs.
Worktrees disabled for sequential single-plan-per-wave phases to avoid per-worktree `pnpm install` overhead; only beneficial when plans have no shared file writes and can run in parallel.
GSD commit helper false-negatives are a known pattern — always follow up with `git log` to confirm the commit landed before reporting success.

The GSD `update-context` tool (not hand-written bash) is the correct way to detect install scope/runtime/version; the main-tree install can be a broken fragment while worktrees hold complete installs.

friction: GSD install in the main tree was a broken fragment (missing gsd-tools.cjs, gsd-context-monitor.js, manifest, most workflows) while worktrees held complete 1.4.3 installs — the discrepancy was non-obvious and required multiple rounds of investigation.
The GSD commit helper consistently false-negatives, requiring a manual `git log` verification step after every commit throughout the session.
1Password SSH signing requires biometric approval per commit, making it incompatible with AFK subagent sessions; had to disable signing globally for the session.
CONTEXT.md cited the wrong test path (`packages/crypto/__tests__/`) which would have caused the TS KAT to be unreachable by vitest — caught only by the researcher subagent reading the vitest config.
The statusline broke silently (blank output, no error surfaced to user) when the repo adopted `"type": "module"` — the CommonJS crash was only diagnosable by running the hook manually.
The GSD installer prompted interactively for keep/remove decisions during the 1.6.0 reinstall, requiring a second non-interactive invocation to complete unattended.
open_items: Wave 4 (61-04: Rust seal variants + full-seal cross-language KAT; 61-05: ADR 0003 + doc pointers) was dispatched but the transcript ends before completion — execution and ship-phase are unfinished.
PR will show a red signature check due to unsigned commits used for the AFK session — needs re-signing or an interactive rebase with signing re-enabled before merge.
`.planning/config.json` is dirty (worktree/chain-flag config toggles set during execution) — needs to be reconciled and committed at session end.
Optional: extend `generate-test-vectors.ts` to auto-generate `node-aad.json` vectors (Phase 61 hand-froze them as the recommended first step; generator extension was explicitly deferred).
GSD .planning/config.json has unknown keys (`created`, `notes`) that the init query warns about on every invocation — benign but worth cleaning up.
GSD worktrees (`fix/phase60-safety-tail`, `fix/fuse-delete-share-revocation`) were removed from disk; their branches still exist and may need eventual cleanup.
